quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What should you do at a school crossing sign?

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mean you are near a school zone or school crossing. Be alert and ready to stop when you see these signs.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Pass slowly.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass quickly and safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass quickly and safely.
questions.explanation: Pass the other vehicle quickly to get back to the normal driving lane. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: On a freeway, why should you look farther ahead than on a city street?

options.text: To spot hazards early.
Because stopping takes a quarter mile.
To keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for traffic changes. Look for signals from other drivers. Expect vehicles merging at on-ramps and be ready for sudden changes in traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: What problem can bad suspension cause?

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and gives a smooth ride. If your vehicle bounces a lot after bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spots.

questions.question: When should you drive on the shoulder to pass a car?

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
Never.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder because the other driver will not expect you there and may pull onto the road. You can only pass on the right if you stay on the roadway.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast a person absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A person's weight, gender, how much food they have eaten, and how many drinks they have had all affect alcohol absorption. The only way to remove alcohol from your system is to wait.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street, start your turn from which lane?

options.text: Any lane, as long as it is safe.
The leftmost lane, closest to the left curb.
The center lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The leftmost lane, closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street to another one-way street, begin your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what should you do?

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at the same time.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap large enough to safely enter the traffic flow. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as other vehicles.
A motorcycle can stop much faster than a regular vehicle.
Motorcycles brake slower than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a regular vehicle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop much faster than regular vehicles. Following too closely puts both your life and the motorcyclist's life at risk. You need enough distance to avoid a crash if the motorcyclist stops suddenly.

questions.question: What should a driver do about the right-of-way?

options.text: Assume all drivers automatically follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way just because of the rules. Always consider the situation and what is happening at the intersection. Yield your right-of-way if it prevents a crash.

questions.question: Which statement about changing lanes is true?

options.text: Only turn and look over your right shoulder for any lane change.
Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
Vehicles with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal and check all mirrors. Then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure the next lane is clear.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates all blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than passenger vehicles.
You can check blind spots using your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Even with rearview and outside mirrors, all vehicles have blind spots. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than regular cars.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, what must you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull over to the edge and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the edge and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop. On one-way streets, drive toward the nearest edge of the road and stop.

questions.question: What is this symbol used for?

options.text: Dangerous intersections.
Slow-moving vehicles.
Yield signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: An orange reflective triangle on the back of a vehicle means it moves slowly. You may see this on farm equipment, roadwork vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. It appears orange during the day and red at night.

questions.question: When driving on a slippery surface like snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Stay close to other vehicles to maintain traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Shift to a low gear before going down a steep hill to prevent skidding. Also, stay farther behind other vehicles than normal. Avoid quick stops. If you do not have antilock brakes, pump the brakes to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which statement about foot placement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply the brakes gently with increasing pressure so your vehicle stops gradually and smoothly.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When the driver you passed signals for you to return.
When you signal your intention for three seconds.
When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure you are not too close to the vehicle you just passed before returning to your lane. When you can see both of the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to return to your lane safely.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid losing traction on wet roads?

options.text: Make abrupt turns.
Apply the brakes firmly.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down on wet roads and keep your tires in good condition to prevent hydroplaning. If you lose control, remove your foot from the gas (do not brake), keep the vehicle straight, and let it slow down gradually.

questions.question: At night, an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on and you cannot see the road. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: You see a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Do not enter until you can drive completely across.
Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter until you can drive completely across.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, only enter the intersection if you can get all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A sharp right turn is ahead.
A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right then sharply left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign means the road will turn sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: When a school bus stops ahead to load or unload children, you must:

options.text: Stop completely until all children leave the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
Change lanes and pass the bus slowly and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, come to a complete stop. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the arm is withdrawn before proceeding. Even after the bus starts moving, do not go until you are sure no children are crossing the road.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for merging traffic if possible.
Speed up to keep your position.
Always maintain your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for merging traffic if possible.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, make room to allow vehicles to merge into your lane.

questions.question: What does excessive speed do?

options.text: Does not increase crash risk.
Improves your ability to react to hazards.
Often leads to risky decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to risky decisions.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of vehicle crashes. It does not save time and often leads to risky decisions.

questions.question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?

options.text: Play the radio loudly to stop thinking about it.
Take a few minutes to cool off.
Drive on the interstate to release your anger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to cool off.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect your driving ability. If you are very angry, excited, afraid, worried, or sad, calm down before driving. You need to focus on driving without thinking about what upset you.

questions.question: Why use headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others of bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, other drivers have difficulty seeing your vehicle. Headlights make your vehicle easier to see. If you need windshield wipers, you must also use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: How can you see objects in your vehicle's blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Check only the left outside mirror.
Look over your left or right shoulder.
Check only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the appropriate shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on snow or ice?

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Make speed and direction changes more gradually than normal.
Drive as you would under normal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make speed and direction changes more gradually than normal.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, change your speed and direction gradually. Never use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may lose grip and you could lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What should drivers do when using a roundabout?

options.text: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Yield to traffic entering the roundabout.
Drive in a clockwise direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with no traffic signal. Traffic flows counterclockwise around a center island. Enter from the right, yield to traffic already in the roundabout, and follow the circle to the right until you reach your exit.
